(papers-designed-on-sky130)=
# Papers naming SKY130 that are not part of the index

Every excluded or held record whose own title or retrieved abstract names
SKY130, the SkyWater 130 nm process or the SkyWater foundry
(`names_process: true` in `data/papers-excluded.yaml`).
They are listed for completeness and are deliberately not part of
{ref}`the index proper <papers-scope>`: none of them meets its inclusion
rules (Sec. 1 of the design). Most report no fabrication or measurement at
all; a few report a measured result on a **different** SkyWater process or
site (S90, a 90 nm node, another fab location) rather than SKY130, or are
excluded for a reason other than a missing measurement (for example, a
slide deck rather than a paper) — each entry's reason says which. A
record shown as **held** is awaiting a full-text check rather than
settled as out of scope.

109 papers name the process out of 154 papers considered
and excluded or held; the rest do not name SKY130 or the SkyWater 130 nm
process anywhere in their own title or abstract.

## 2026

Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research), 2026. [10.5281/zenodo.18821107](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18821107). Self-published Zenodo survey of open-source EDA/AI trends; mentions "the release of the SkyWater 130nm and GlobalFoundries 180nm PDKs" as ecosystem background, with no circuit or fabrication result of its own.

[arxiv:2606.05253](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05253). Reports an area-delay-product reduction "under Sky130" from synthesis-derived PPA rewards in an RTL-optimization agent; no fabrication.
* **An Agentic LLM Flow for Chip Timing Closure: Cross-Stage Context Propagation in EDA**. Gursimran S Sodhi. Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research), 2026. [10.5281/zenodo.20032068](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20032068). Self-published Zenodo EDA-methodology article; evaluates an LLM timing-closure flow on OpenROAD benchmark designs said to use the SkyWater 130nm PDK, measuring only synthesis/STA metrics (WNS), with no fabrication. No longer retrievable as of 2026-09-25 (confirmed dead on both the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-25 checks); no Wayback or archive.today snapshot found anywhere; evidence for this description is now weak, resting only on the record as it read before it went offline.
* **An Open-Source LFSR-Based Stochastic Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron in SkyWater 130 nm: Design, Stochastic Characterisation, and Rate Coding**. Poornima Kumaresan and Santhosh Sivasubramani. arXiv, 2026. [arxiv:2606.23532](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23532). Stochastic LIF neuron "in standard-cell CMOS on the SkyWater 130 nm process", sized for a Tiny Tapeout tile; the abstract states explicitly "All results are pre-silicon, from simulation and the open flow." Companion of arxiv:2606.22635 by the same authors.
* **Analysis of Floorplan Utilization and Routing Congestion in RTL-to-GDSII Implementation of the PicoRV32 RISC-V Core Using SKY130 Technology**. Dr. Narayana Swamy J C Chetan V. Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research), 2026. [10.5281/zenodo.20594749](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20594749). * **Ankhdjet: An Open-Source Compiler for Mask-Programmed Ternary Compute-in-ROM on an Open PDK**. Mohnish Pai. arXiv, 2026. [arxiv:2608.26206](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26206). A compute-in-ROM macro compiled for a future SKY130 Tiny Tapeout/ChipFoundry shuttle ("silicon expected 2027"); the abstract's own reported numbers are from extracted-parasitic simulation and it states no energy measurements are claimed.

All-digital PLL run through the OpenLane RTL-to-GDSII flow "incorporated with the open-source Sky130 Process Design Kit"; the abstract reports gate-level post-layout simulation only and states the GDS "can be sent to foundries", i.e. not yet fabricated.
* **Open-Source Chip Design in Academic Education**. Syed Anas Alam, Jakob Furbo Enevoldsen, Andreas Alkjaer Eriksen, Niels William Hartmann, Ulrik Helk, Jorgen Kragh Jakobsen, Christa Skytte Jensen, Nicolai Dyre Bulow Jespersen, Karl Herman Krause, Mads Rumle Nordstrom, Tjark Petersen, Luca Pezzarossa, Simon Winther Rasmussen, Martin Schoeberl and Jonas Ingerslev Sorensen. 2022 IEEE Nordic Circuits and Systems Conference (NorCAS), 2022. [10.1109/norcas57515.2022.9934685](https://doi.org/10.1109/norcas57515.2022.9934685). DTU BSc course chip "using open-source tools and the SkyWater process"; the abstract says the project "has recently achieved tape-out for the next multi-project wafer manufacturing" with no measurement yet reported.

## 2021

* **A CMOS Programmable Analog Standard Cell Library in Skywater 130nm Open-Source Process**. authors not recorded. WOSET, 2021. Workshop precursor of the included IEEE TCAS-I 2024 library paper; the PDF says the cells "are in process for fabrication", so it has no silicon results.
* **A Highly Digital VCO-based ADC for IoT Applications on Skywater 130nm**. Duc-Manh Tran, Ngo-Doanh Nguyen, Duy-Hieu Bui and Xuan-Tu Tran. 2021 8th NAFOSTED Conference on Information and Computer Science (NICS), 2021. [10.1109/nics54270.2021.9701515](https://doi.org/10.1109/nics54270.2021.9701515). "Implemented and verified by fully open-source tools" reads as simulation-only; no fabrication or measurement is stated.
* **Enabling Reusable Physical Design Flows with Modular Flow Generators**. Alex Carsello, James Thomas, Ankita Nayak, Po-Han Chen, Mark Horowitz, Priyanka Raina and Christopher Torng. arXiv, 2021. [arxiv:2111.14535](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14535). A flow-reuse tooling paper (mflowgen) evaluated across five technology nodes (TSMC16/28/40, SKY130, IBM180); the abstract reports no SKY130-specific process or silicon findings. Also published as doi:10.1145/3489517.3530633 (ICCAD 2022).
* **Taping out an FPGA in 24 hours with OpenFPGA: The SOFA Project**. Xifan Tang, Ganesh Gore, Grant Brown and Pierre-Emmanuel Gaillardon. 2021 31st International Conference on Field-Programmable Logic and Applications (FPL), 2021. [10.1109/fpl53798.2021.00085](https://doi.org/10.1109/fpl53798.2021.00085). Skywater Open-source embedded FpgAs (SOFA) project, a series of open-source embedded FPGA IPs built with the Skywater 130nm technology; the abstract reports only "fabrication-ready layouts" generated in 24 hours, no measured silicon result. The open-source-eFPGA sibling of the included FABulous SKY130 paper.
